subject.title: Feature Request: Enforce skill execution sandbox when enabled: false

question: Should `skills.entries.<key>.enabled:false` become a hard read/exec access boundary for that skill, or should hard skill isolation use a separate strict policy while `enabled:false` remains an eligibility toggle?
rationale: The fix changes public disabled-skill semantics and can affect existing trusted workflows, while the durable security boundary crosses skill loading, filesystem tools, exec, sandboxing, Gateway/UI status, and docs.

options.title: Make disabled a hard boundary
options.body: Treat `enabled:false` as a deny policy for skill files and scripts, with upgrade notes and tests for read, exec, sandbox, UI, and docs behavior.

options.title: Add a separate strict isolation policy
options.body: Keep `enabled:false` as a visibility/eligibility toggle and introduce an explicit strict skill isolation control for operators who need enforcement.

options.title: Document current semantics only
options.body: Clarify that disabling a skill removes it from invocation surfaces but does not isolate host files or shell execution, and point users to sandboxing/tool-deny/OS isolation.

recommendation.title: Make disabled a hard boundary
recommendation.body: Treat `enabled:false` as a deny policy for skill files and scripts, with upgrade notes and tests for read, exec, sandbox, UI, and docs behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the clearest local history owner for the active skill filtering, skill security, and exec boundary surfaces involved in this choice.
